news.story_lead: Maharashtra plans cochlear implant facility for patients with hearing impairment in all municipal hospitals At present, the Thane Municipal Corporation provides the facility, and the Maharashtra government is planning to expand it across other municipal corporations. The Maharashtra government is considering setting up cochlear implant surgery facilities for deaf patients, along with early detection and treatment services, in municipal corporation hospitals across the state. At present, the Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC) provides the facility, and along similar lines, the state government is planning to expand it across other municipal corporations.
news.full_article_text: Maharashtra plans cochlear implant facility for patients with hearing impairment in all municipal hospitals At present, the Thane Municipal Corporation provides the facility, and the Maharashtra government is planning to expand it across other municipal corporations. The Maharashtra government is considering setting up cochlear implant surgery facilities for deaf patients, along with early detection and treatment services, in municipal corporation hospitals across the state. At present, the Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC) provides the facility, and along similar lines, the state government is planning to expand it across other municipal corporations. Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde said he would discuss the proposal with chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and public health minister Prakashrao Abitkar to ensure that children with hearing impairments receive timely diagnosis and treatment at municipal hospitals across Maharashtra. A cochlear implant is a small, complex electronic medical device that provides a sense of sound to people who are deaf or have severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss. Unlike hearing aids, which amplify sound, cochlear implants bypass damaged hair cells in the inner ear and directly stimulate the auditory nerve through electrical signals, helping individuals perceive sound. Shinde was speaking at a Diwali gathering organised at Nandanvan, his official residence at Malabar Hill, for children who have undergone heart and cochlear implant surgeries and their parents. He said the Thane Municipal Corporation had already introduced cochlear implant surgery facilities, benefiting several children. A portion of the expenditure for these surgeries was borne by the Chief Minister's Relief Fund. The civic body has now also started facilities for early diagnosis. "If surgery is performed at the right time, a child can develop the ability to hear and speak, changing the course of their entire life. Therefore, providing these facilities is a need of the hour and a social responsibility," Shinde said. Shinde also cited examples of beneficiaries who had gone on to achieve remarkable success. One girl who underwent cochlear implant surgery secured admission to IIT, while another boy was selected for the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), he said. He said that Shiv Sena Medical Help Cell and the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation had been supporting families of children with hearing disabilities and heart conditions for the past nine years. The initiative has reached 28 districts, with teams visiting villages from Gadchiroli to Sangli to identify children requiring medical intervention. Children were brought to Mumbai for surgeries.

news.full_article_text: SC rejects bail plea of doctor accused of prescribing cough syrup linked to 26 child deaths New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to grant bail to paediatrician Praveen Soni, who was arrested in October 2025 for allegedly continuing to prescribe Coldrif cough syrup linked to the deaths of 26 children in Madhya Pradesh, observing that the case was too serious to warrant his release at this stage New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to grant bail to paediatrician Praveen Soni, who was arrested in October 2025 for allegedly continuing to prescribe Coldrif cough syrup linked to the deaths of 26 children in Madhya Pradesh, observing that the case was too serious to warrant his release at this stage. A bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, declined to entertain the plea, pointing out that charges had been framed against Soni only recently and that the stockist involved in the case was his relative, suggesting possible connections that required closer scrutiny. “This is not a case of bail. You will have to wait. Charges have been framed just recently. And the stockist happens to be your relative. There are some connections,” the bench told senior advocate Siddhartha Dave, appearing for Soni. When Dave argued that his client had only prescribed the medicine and was neither its manufacturer nor involved in its production, the bench underscored the gravity of the allegations, particularly given his professional qualifications. “Children died...it is very serious. Twenty-six children died. The fact that you are a qualified doctor is all the more serious,” remarked the bench. The court further observed that unless the prosecution was unable to establish the requisite knowledge on Soni’s part, the case could attract a punishment of life imprisonment. “Unless you can prove absence of requisite knowledge, it is a case of life imprisonment,” said the court, before dismissing the petition. The court, however, permitted Soni to renew his bail plea after a year. Soni, who was posted at the Civil Hospital in Parasia in Madhya Pradesh’s Chhindwara district, was arrested on October 5, 2025, following a complaint by the block medical officer, Dr Ankit Sehlam. He faces charges under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), besides provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. The first child death linked to Coldrif was reported in Chhindwara on September 4, 2025. However, the syrup allegedly continued to be prescribed even as more cases emerged. Investigations subsequently revealed the presence of diethylene glycol (DEG), a toxic industrial solvent, in alarmingly high concentrations in samples of the medicine. Laboratory reports cited by the prosecution found DEG levels of up to 46.28% weight by volume in the syrup, against the permissible limit of 0.1%. The chemical, commonly used in industrial products such as brake fluid and antifreeze, can cause acute kidney injury and potentially fatal kidney failure, particularly in children. According to the prosecution, children between two and four years of age were prescribed the syrup by Soni, following which they developed acute kidney injuries and were referred to a medical college hospital in Nagpur, where several died. The prosecution has alleged that Soni’s wife, Jyoti Soni, who was working at Apna Medical Store, a pharmacy owned by her husband and located adjacent to his clinic, sold the syrup without prescriptions. It further alleged that Soni received a 10% commission on every bottle prescribed, while the pharmacy earned a profit of ₹ 23 per bottle, pointing to an alleged arrangement between the couple to prescribe and sell the medicine. The state also alleged that Soni continued prescribing the syrup despite a December 18, 2023 circular issued by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization prohibiting fixed-dose combination cough syrups for children below four years of age. The prosecution further claimed that he had been cautioned by a senior paediatrician in Nagpur about a similar tragedy involving DEG-contaminated cough syrup in Delhi in 1998. Soni’s defence has maintained that he was neither the manufacturer nor involved in the production of the syrup, which was manufactured by Sresan Pharmaceuticals Ltd under a valid licence. His counsel also argued that the medicine had not been banned when it was prescribed and relied on the Supreme Court’s 2005 judgment in Jacob Mathew v State of Punjab, which laid down safeguards against criminal prosecution of medical practitioners without appropriate expert opinion. The Madhya Pradesh high court had rejected Soni’s second bail application on June 30, 2026, holding that there was no change in circumstances since his first bail plea was dismissed on February 17, except for the additional period spent in custody. In the report submitted to the government on Friday, Rao also mentioned that Excise Minister M Liju was acquainted with one of the bar owners allegedly involved in the transactions. The report also flagged allegations against Alappuzha Deputy Commissioner Ajay. According to the information received by Rao, the owner of Roma Centre Bar at Kattachira in Kayamkulam was allegedly asked to pay ₹ 30,000 during the deputy commissioner's inspection visits, it said. The report identified the bar owner as Ratheesh and stated that he was known to the Excise Minister. It also mentioned an alleged payment of ₹ 20,000 after Onam this year in connection with the renewal of the bar's licence in April. Rao recommended that Vinod and Ajay be immediately removed from field postings and transferred to offices such as the Excise Crime Records Bureau or Toddy Board. He also recommended a vigilance inquiry into the allegations of bribe collection, monthly payments and disproportionate assets against the two officials under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act. The report further called for stricter controls on posting officials facing allegations of financial irregularities to sensitive locations and establishments, and recommended that future transfers and appointments at the JEC, Additional Excise Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner levels be considered based on reports from the Excise Commissioner. news.full_article_text: As tracks pierce isolated red region, Chhattisgarh’s Abujhmad finds a route to progress A new railway line connecting Rowghat to Dallirajhara in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar region promises faster, cheaper travel, better access to education, healthcare At around 6.30 in the morning of a late October day, a train with around 30 passengers leaves the station at Rowghat, in Chhattisgarh’s Kanker district. It will pick up more at Tadoki, Antagarh, Bhanupratappur, and Kewti, before reaching its destination, Dallirajhara, around 100km away. The 12-carriage train soon enters a dense forest; the morning sunlight falls through the trees as the train rolls past hills, streams and small settlements. The beauty of the landscape is not lost on siblings Anil Potai and Anjani Potai, students of Swami Atmanand College in Raipur and residents of Narayanpur. “There are streams almost every kilometre . It is so beautiful,” Anjani says, recording the landscape on her phone. Her brother Anil reflects on what the rail link could mean. “Earlier, it used to take the whole day to reach Raipur. Now, I can reach there in a few hours. I am sure that many tribal youths will now study in Raipur,” he says. At Tadoki, five security personnel board the train, a reminder of the violence that wreaked the region not so long ago; at 7.30am, the train reaches Antagarh, where another 50 people board, most headed for mining town of Dalli Rajhara in Balod district. One of the security personnel, whose name is being withheld for security reasons, is travelling to his village in Bihar for Diwali. He says the situation has improved considerably and that there is little to worry about once the train crosses Antagarh. “But here, fear is still there,” he says. Punem, a resident of Antagarh travelling to Dallirajhara for a family function, says the train is cheaper and faster than other options. He plans to return by the same train. From Kewti, about 15km from Antagarh, farmer Kaushal Baghel boards the train for Raipur, saying it has made medical care more accessible. “The train has made it easier to reach Raipur. Earlier, it was an 8-10 hour bus journey. Now, I can go for my knee consultation at a Raipur hospital,” he says. As more passengers board, people chat in local languages, click pictures and play music on their phones. For some older passengers, it is their first train journey. Construction for the 95km Dallirajhara–Rowghatt railway line, which has 26 operational stations between Raipur and Rowghat, began in 2015. The 75km stretch up to Tadoki was completed in 2023, with passenger train services commencing the same year. The remaining was constructed over the next three years. On October 20, 2026, state chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai and Union railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw inaugurated the railway line. Train to Maoist heartland It is 6am, inside a forest in Chhattisgarh’s Kanker district, where a 12-coach passenger train is parked at the platform of the newly built Rowghat railway station, once a Maoist bastion, surrounded by serene hills and dense forests. Its two platforms are protected by security camps providing round-the-clock cover, although no Maoist violence has been reported in the region for the past seven months. The central government has claimed it wiped out Maoism in Chhattisgarh by March 31, 2026. Since January 2024, security forces have killed 493 Maoists in a series of encounters, while 2,793 Communist Party of India (Maoist) leaders and cadres have surrendered. Rowghat, 140km from Kanker district headquarters, is the first passenger railway station in Abujhmad, once considered an impregnable bastion of Left-wing extremism. The train passes through places such as Tadoki, once a hotbed of Maoist violence. A few passengers from nearby villages wait for the train to depart as station master MK Sahu sips his morning tea. “On average, about 40 people board the train from Rowghat every day, although the number touched 70 one day after the service started on October 20,” he says. #### मुख्य रणनीतिक विवरण
- **भूमिगत बुनियादी ढांचा:** ईरानी सशस्त्र बल मिसाइल निर्माण, भंडारण और प्रक्षेपण प्रणालियों को सुरक्षित रखने के लिए मजबूत भूमिगत प्रतिष्ठानों का निर्माण कर रहे हैं, जिससे हवाई बमबारी से होने वाले नुकसान को कम किया जा सके।

news.full_article_text: - Published 6 November 2026, 15:04 GMT Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have been climbing following an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index opened higher following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday. Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development. However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September. On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers. But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, up 1.4%, reversing some of its 5.5% fall. The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, was up about 0.7%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day. Nvidia shed hundreds of billions in market value on Thursday after shares slid more than 9%, but recovered some of those losses on Friday, trading up more than 3%. SpaceX and Tesla shares, which were also hammered on Thursday, saw mixed gains, up more than 8% and nearly 5% respectively. Chipmakers AMD and Micron both dropped by more than 17% on Thursday, but AMD shares had risen by about 10% on Friday while Micron was up more than 5%. However, stock markets in Asia and Europe fared worse on Friday. The Kospi in South Korea closed down 6% on Friday, with shares in chipmaker SK Hynix plunging more than 10%. European markets also fell, with the main indexes in Germany, France and Spain ending the day down. In the UK, the FTSE 100, which tracks the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, declined 1.01%. In addition to the recent market volatility, UK traders were also digesting the latest Bank of England decision to raise interest rates and the signal that another rate rise could be on the cards to curb rising prices. Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said it had been a brutal week for markets, and the key question was whether the jump in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq would be sustained. "While no-one knows what happens next, it's clear that we've just seen a significant shift in market sentiment," he said. "Once investors have had the weekend to catch their breath, next week could give a clearer indication of whether the tech trade is going down the pan or fighting back." - Could the US midterms put a pin in the AI bubble? A number of Democrats campaigned for new rules and regulations for artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres, and the party has since won control of both houses of congress as well as key contests in states that have been part of the AI data centre race. US President Donald Trump on Friday reiterated his supported for what he calls "super intelligence", saying only "foolish leadership" would "say no to the riches they bring". However, there have also been concerns over whether the enormous amounts of money being spent on AI will pay off. Russ Shaw, founder of global tech advocacy firm Tech London Advocates, said the election result was sending a message that a rethink was needed on AI. "The incoming Congress is going to really focus on AI in a very dramatic way," he told the BBC's Business Today. "I'm a big fan of AI, but I'm watching what these companies are doing, and they're not communicating effectively at all, particularly in the US, about what the benefits of AI are all about." He said people were watching firms come into their communities and build data centres while their own energy costs were going up, and those companies "have to be better neighbours". Strong jobs figures could ease market fears As well as the fallout of the midterms and the plunge in artificial intelligence stocks, US traders will also be digesting the latest jobs figures. And those numbers were better than expected: US employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, well above the average monthly increase and more than double what analysts had expected. Overall the unemployment rate, which counts the number of people who are out of work but actively looking for a job, eased slightly to 4.1% from 4.2% in September . The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the unemployment rate has remained in the narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March. Neil Birrell, chief investment officer at investment firm Premier Miton, said while the jobs figures may feel like second billing to the market movements they were still important. "The US economy is running hard which may mean the risks the markets are worrying about at the moment are not such a risk to the real economy as is being feared," he said. news.story_lead: Rajasthan: Kuno forest team tracking cheetah KGP-3 attacked by villagers after it kills buffalo calf A Kuno National Park forester alleged that villagers assaulted and tried to strangle him while his team tracked cheetah KGP-3 in Rajasthan’s Karauli district. A forest team from Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park, deployed to track the movements of cheetah KGP-3 after it strayed into Rajasthan’s Karauli district, was allegedly assaulted by a group of villagers following the animal’s killing of a buffalo calf, police said on Friday. A forester sustained injuries and sought police protection for the team, which is monitoring the cheetah in the Mandrayal area.
news.full_article_text: Rajasthan: Kuno forest team tracking cheetah KGP-3 attacked by villagers after it kills buffalo calf A Kuno National Park forester alleged that villagers assaulted and tried to strangle him while his team tracked cheetah KGP-3 in Rajasthan’s Karauli district. A forest team from Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park, deployed to track the movements of cheetah KGP-3 after it strayed into Rajasthan’s Karauli district, was allegedly assaulted by a group of villagers following the animal’s killing of a buffalo calf, police said on Friday. A forester sustained injuries and sought police protection for the team, which is monitoring the cheetah in the Mandrayal area. Alok Prajapati (34), a forester with Kuno National Park, lodged a complaint on Tuesday against five to six unidentified villagers for allegedly assaulting members of the forest team. In his complaint, Prajapati said that the cheetah’s movement had been traced to the area under Chandelipura gram panchayat of Mandrayal police station limits, where the animal had killed a buffalo calf. Around five to six villagers allegedly approached the team and began abusing its members. They assaulted Prajapati and threatened to kill him, according to the complaint. Prajapati also sought police security for the forest team deployed for night patrolling. Prajapati told HT that an elderly man approached the team while it was patrolling the area to track the cheetah’s movements and started abusing them. “We tried to convince him and assured him that compensation would be provided for the death of the buffalo calf. Later, another man arrived and called other villagers. The attackers tried to strangle me and started pelting stones,” he alleged. Mandrayal police station station house officer Jay Prakash Singh said a case had been registered against five to six unidentified people under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). An investigation is underway to identify the accused and initiate legal action, he said.

A forest team from Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park, deployed to track the movements of cheetah KGP-3 after it strayed into Rajasthan’s Karauli district, was allegedly assaulted by a group of villagers following the animal’s killing of a buffalo calf, police said on Friday. A forester sustained injuries and sought police protection for the team, which is monitoring the cheetah in the Mandrayal area.

A forest team from Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park, deployed to track the movements of cheetah KGP-3 after it strayed into Rajasthan’s Karauli district, was allegedly assaulted by a group of villagers following the animal’s killing of a buffalo calf, police said on Friday. A forester sustained injuries and sought police protection for the team, which is monitoring the cheetah in the Mandrayal area. Alok Prajapati (34), a forester with Kuno National Park, lodged a complaint on Tuesday against five to six unidentified villagers for allegedly assaulting members of the forest team. In his complaint, Prajapati said that the cheetah’s movement had been traced to the area under Chandelipura gram panchayat of Mandrayal police station limits, where the animal had killed a buffalo calf. Around five to six villagers allegedly approached the team and began abusing its members. They assaulted Prajapati and threatened to kill him, according to the complaint. Prajapati also sought police security for the forest team deployed for night patrolling. Prajapati told HT that an elderly man approached the team while it was patrolling the area to track the cheetah’s movements and started abusing them. “We tried to convince him and assured him that compensation would be provided for the death of the buffalo calf. Later, another man arrived and called other villagers. The attackers tried to strangle me and started pelting stones,” he alleged. Mandrayal police station station house officer Jay Prakash Singh said a case had been registered against five to six unidentified people under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). An investigation is underway to identify the accused and initiate legal action, he said.

news.full_article_text: Supreme Court appoints ex-CJI Gavai to head panel scrutinising forest rights claims in Tamil Nadu The Supreme Court has tasked a panel led by ex-CJI Bhushan Gavai with scrutinising forest rights claims under the FRA in Tamil Nadu. The Supreme Court on Friday appointed former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Bhushan R Gavai to head a special committee that will scrutinise orders passed by authorities in Tamil Nadu under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 (FRA), even as it came down hard on the state government for its prolonged failure to initiate the statutory process to identify and adjudicate the claims of forest dwellers in the ecologically sensitive Agasthyamalai landscape. A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta constituted the committee, comprising Justice Gavai as chairperson, an officer of the Central Empowered Committee (CEC) and Tamil Nadu’s principal chief conservator of forests, to oversee the determination of claims by Forest-Dwelling Scheduled Tribe (FDST) and other traditional forest dwellers (OTFD). The committee will scrutinise the orders passed by competent authorities under the FRA and submit its findings to the court in a sealed cover. The court directed the state to complete the constitution of the remaining Gram Sabhas within 30 days and conclude the entire process of inviting and adjudicating claims through the statutory three-tier mechanism within five months of their constitution. The committee, in turn, has been asked to complete its scrutiny within two months of the expiry of this outer deadline. Criticising the state for its inaction, the bench observed that the process under the FRA had remained uninitiated for years even after an interim stay imposed by the Madras high court was vacated by the Supreme Court in 2016. “Apparently thus, the process under Section 6 was never initiated for years even after the lifting of the stay and seems to have been triggered only after this Court took suo motu cognizance of the prevailing situation,” it said. The bench added that the state appeared to have “woken up” only after the court directed the removal of encroachments from the Srivilliputhur-Megamalai Tiger Reserve and other reserved forests in the Agasthyamalai Biosphere. “It is clear that the State Government is primarily responsible for the delay in the process of receiving, identifying and adjudicating the claims under the FRA, 2006. Before this Court took cognizance of the encroachments in the forest area, even the Gram Sabhas had not been constituted,” said the bench, granting the state what it described as a “last opportunity” to complete the exercise. The committee has been empowered to issue necessary directions to authorities for expeditious disposal of claims. The state will also have to submit monthly progress reports to it. Senior counsel Jaideep Gupta appeared for the state government, while senior advocate Sriram Panchu represented the state’s department of Social Justice. The directions came in proceedings concerning large-scale encroachments in the Agasthyamalai landscape, where the court had, in its May 29 judgment, ordered a structured and time-bound process for eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration. The latest proceedings arose from competing claims over the application of the FRA to people residing in or cultivating land in the Megamalai region. While the state argued that claims under the FRA needed to be examined before eviction, the court accepted the amicus curiae and senior advocate K Parmeshwar’s submission that the statutory protection could not be extended indiscriminately to everyone occupying or cultivating forest land. The bench clarified that two categories of occupants identified by the state itself would be excluded from consideration under the Act. These are people cultivating forest land while maintaining only temporary residence within it and those residing outside the forest boundary but cultivating land inside it. The state’s affidavit had identified 4,594 occupants spread across 5,072.64 hectares, of whom 2,643 were engaged in silk cotton cultivation over 3,637.83 hectares. Of these, 1,595 persons were permanently residing in the forest and cultivating land, 232 had temporary residence while cultivating, and 2,767 were residing outside the forest boundary but cultivating within it. The court said the latter two categories could not qualify as FDST or OTFD merely on the basis of cultivation, since the statutory definitions required claimants to primarily reside in and depend on forest land. For OTFDs, the law specifically requires residence and dependence for at least three generations, or 75 years, prior to December 13, 2005. The court also rejected the state’s attempt to justify silk cotton cultivation as a traditional minor forest produce protected under the FRA. It noted that the government had relied on historical cultivation and agricultural records but had failed to produce any specific notification recognising silk cotton as minor forest produce under the Act or any other forest law. Distinguishing between naturally occurring forest produce and commercial cultivation, the bench said the material suggested that silk cotton had been introduced as a planned plantation rather than traditionally collected as minor forest produce. “The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crop is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce,” said the bench, adding that commercial crop cultivation could not become a recognised forest right to justify continued occupation of reserved forest land. It further asked the CEC to examine the state’s claim that silk cotton qualified as minor forest produce and investigate the circumstances surrounding cultivation by people residing outside the forest boundary, including whether others were financing or facilitating such activity. The matter will next be heard on February 1, 2027, when the court will consider an interim status report. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. news.headline: Satellite Imagery Reveals Iranian Underground Expansion and Repairs at Key Missile Bases
news.story_lead: Analysis of November 2026 satellite imagery indicates that Iran is actively repairing damaged military complexes and constructing new subterranean facilities near its major missile bases. According to intelligence analysts, these activities at locations such as Karaj, Shahroud, and Parchin aim to fortify missile production and storage capacity against air strikes.
news.full_article_text:
### Satellite Analysis of Iranian Military Infrastructure

Recent satellite imagery analyzed by British intelligence firm MAIAR, with additional evaluations from Janes and the Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI), reveals ongoing construction and repair activities across strategic Iranian military facilities. Despite extensive US and Israeli air strikes targeting defense complexes, Iranian forces are restoring damaged structures and expanding underground networks to safeguard critical military assets.

### Primary Sites Under Repair and Construction

- **Garmdareh Military Base (Karaj):** Located near Tehran, satellite imagery shows excavation, vehicle movement, and newly constructed portals for an underground facility.
- **Shahroud Base:** Situated in northern Iran, digging and new building construction indicate efforts by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to relocate missile manufacturing facilities underground.
- **Parchin Military Complex:** East of Tehran, debris from previous air strikes has been cleared. At the Taleghan 2 facility within Parchin, an underground bunker has been repaired and reinforced with concrete.
- **Kermanshah Missile Base:** Located in western Iran near the border with Iraq, destroyed facilities have been covered with new roofs.
- **Fordo Region (Qom):** Excavations and construction work have been observed outside tunnel entrances close to the Fordo underground uranium enrichment facility.

### Strategic Implications and Expert Findings

Defense analysts, including former CIA analyst Jim Lamson and CSIS expert Mark Cancian, note that Iran is prioritizing military capability reconstruction and underground fortification over economic rehabilitation. Transitioning military manufacturing and storage into subterranean facilities reduces visibility for foreign satellite intelligence and mitigates vulnerability to precision aerial attacks.
news.background_context: Months of US and Israeli air strikes targeted Iranian drone, ballistic missile, and naval sites, with US Pentagon estimates stating that up to 90% of Iran's drone, missile, and naval industrial base had been degraded. Iran has historically utilized underground bunker networks to protect its strategic assets.

hindi_translation.story_lead: नवंबर 2026 के उपग्रह चित्रों के विश्लेषण से पता चलता है कि ईरान प्रमुख मिसाइल ठिकानों के पास क्षतिग्रस्त सैन्य बुनियादी ढांचे की मरम्मत कर रहा है और नई भूमिगत सुविधाएं बना रहा है। खुफिया विश्लेषकों का संकेत है कि करज, शाहरूद और परचिन जैसे स्थलों पर इन प्रयासों का उद्देश्य अमेरिकी और इजराइली हवाई हमलों से मिसाइल उत्पादन और भंडारण की रक्षा करना है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### ईरानी सैन्य बुनियादी ढांचे पर उपग्रह विश्लेषण

ब्रिटिश इंटेलिजेंस कंपनी MAIAR द्वारा विश्लेषित और जेन्स (Janes) तथा फॉरेन पॉलिसी रिसर्च इंस्टीट्यूट (FPRI) के इनपुट वाले हालिया उपग्रह चित्र प्रमुख ईरानी सैन्य सुविधाओं में महत्वपूर्ण निर्माण और मरम्मत गतिविधियों को उजागर करते हैं। अमेरिकी और इजराइली हवाई हमलों से कई रक्षा परिसरों को नुकसान पहुंचने के बावजूद, ईरानी बल सक्रिय रूप से अपने ठिकानों को बहाल कर रहे हैं और परिचालन क्षमताओं की सुरक्षा के लिए भूमिगत बुनियादी ढांचे का निर्माण कर रहे हैं।

### मरम्मत और निर्माण के तहत प्राथमिक स्थल

- **गर्मदारेह सैन्य अड्डा (करज):** तेहरान के पास स्थित, उपग्रह तस्वीरें उत्खनन, वाहनों की आवाजाही और नए सुरंग द्वारों को दर्शाती हैं जो एक भूमिगत सुविधा के निर्माण का संकेत देते हैं।
- **शाहरूद अड्डा:** उत्तरी ईरान में स्थित, खुदाई और नई संरचनाएं दर्शाती हैं कि इस्लामिक रिवोल्यूशनरी गार्ड कॉर्प्स (IRGC) मिसाइल उत्पादन सुविधाओं को भूमिगत स्थानांतरित करने का प्रयास कर रही है।
- **परचिन सैन्य परिसर:** तेहरान के पूर्व में स्थित, क्षतिग्रस्त संरचनाओं को साफ कर दिया गया है, और तालेघान 2 स्थल पर महत्वपूर्ण कार्यों में एक भूमिगत बंकर की कंक्रीट सुदृढ़ीकरण मरम्मत शामिल है।
- **केरमनशाह मिसाइल अड्डा:** इराक सीमा के पास पश्चिमी ईरान में स्थित, नष्ट हुई सुविधाओं पर नए रूफ (छत) लगाए गए हैं।
- **फोर्दो क्षेत्र (कोम):** फोर्दो भूमिगत यूरेनियम संवर्धन स्थल के पास सुरंग द्वारों के बाहर नए उत्खनन और निर्माण कार्य दर्ज किए गए हैं।

### रणनीतिक निहितार्थ और विशेषज्ञ निष्कर्ष

पूर्व सीआईए विश्लेषक जिम लेमसन और सीएसआईएस सैन्य विशेषज्ञ मार्क कैनसियन सहित रक्षा विश्लेषकों का कहना है कि ईरान आर्थिक पुनर्वास की तुलना में सैन्य क्षमता के पुनर्निर्माण और भूमिगत सुदृढ़ीकरण को प्राथमिकता दे रहा है। बुनियादी ढांचे को भूमिगत स्थानांतरित करने से विदेशी उपग्रह निगरानी जटिल हो जाती है और भविष्य के हवाई हमलों से परिसंपत्तियों की सुरक्षा होती है।
